cells.gaps: No row says which tiers enter routine aggregate reports, where clinics' reports are keyed, or how many primary clinics enter their own; the one digitised fact (2022) is hospitals and maternities recording births and deaths, and it disagrees with the 2019 profile's statement of no electronic aggregation (SWZ-032). No plan or finance fact falls inside the 36 months; the only plan fact is from 2019.
cells.note: Digital entry is evidenced at hospitals only, with DHIS2 introduced nationally in 2024 and no tier of use stated. Stage 3 needs a system keyed at district taking the clinics' reports, which no row shows.

cells.gaps: The 73% (233 sites, 2026) and the 75% (247 of 327, March 2024, SWZ-020) are shares of all health facilities, with no count of primary clinics alone; the 2024 report gives point-of-care with the Master Patient Index not live (SWZ-022), against shared in 2026. The newest governance fact (SWZ-035, October 2026) names the ministry's HMIS programme as technical lead, after the US State Department had ownership of CMIS passing to the government in FY2026 (SWZ-034, May 2026); no current plan naming CMIS and no domestic budget line has been found from an admitted source, the only plan row (SWZ-007) being from the excluded compilation.
cells.note: Records are shared at the point of care on a unique ID, but the 73% is a share of all health facilities, which does not settle rung 4 (Bill, 2026-10-23), and no share or count of primary clinics alone has been found. Governance would cap the cell at 3 in any case, finance being donor only with no current plan.
